content.text: I've reviewed the entire agreement. There is no audit, inspection, records-examination or usage-verification right anywhere in it, and searches for "audit", "records", "inspect" and "verif" return nothing.

input.quote: Customer agrees to provide all reasonable and necessary access, support and cooperation for Kubient to provide the Services in a timely and effective manner.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no audit, inspection, records-examination or usage-verification right exercisable against the Customer (AP). Full-text searches for "audit", "records", "inspect" and "verif" return no hits, and a read of every paragraph of the single section confirms it: the fees provision (§5, p0023) creates no examination right, and the only access-related obligation on AP (§1, p0001) is cooperation for Kubient to deliver the Services, not a right to audit AP's books, usage or systems. That outcome is better than the preferred position (annual audits, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, Vendor cost, no system access) because Kubient has no audit right at all, so there is no frequency, notice, cost-allocation or system-access exposure to constrain. No redline is warranted; inserting audit machinery would create an obligation against us that does not currently exist. Separately noted for the deal team (not a deviation under this rule): Impressions are measured solely "as measured by Kubient" (p0009) and revenue share is per Exhibit with no AP-side reporting or verification right — an AP audit right over Kubient's reporting would be beneficial to us and can be raised under the reporting/revenue-verification rule rather than here.
